results.description:
No. The US is not building a military base in Nigeria.

Nigerian Defence Headquarters, the National Security Adviser, and AFRICOM officials have repeatedly confirmed there are no plans for any foreign military base. A temporary group of about 200 US personnel arrived in early 2026 for training, advisory, and intelligence support at existing Nigerian sites like Bauchi Airfield. They operated under Nigerian control and were largely withdrawn by August 2026.

Cooperation continues through joint operations, equipment, and intel sharing, but no permanent US base exists or is under construction.

results.description:
#ThisWeekinUSNigeriaHistory in 1999, Secretary of State Madeleine K. Albright visited Nigeria and met with President Olusegun Obasanjo and other senior Nigerian officials at an important moment in United States-Nigeria relations.

The visit advanced practical cooperation on trade and investment, education, public health, and regional security. Today, the United States continues to engage Nigeria on shared priorities including expanding commercial opportunities, strengthening security cooperation, protecting religious freedom, and advancing regional peace and stability.

Photo credit: Gettyimages

results.title: Hours after Indigenous youth leaders in Nigeria's Plateau State credited U.S.-backed counterterrorism ops with saving thousands of lives, te
results.description:
Hours after Indigenous youth leaders in Nigeria's Plateau State credited U.S.-backed counterterrorism ops with saving thousands of lives, terrorists killed 1 person in a farming village south of Jos the state capital.

The coalition says 152 Christian villages have been seized in 20 years. A local bishop says the Army's swift response last night prevented more deaths.

Solomon Dalyop, who spoke on behalf of the Plateau youth leaders during a press conference in Abuja, Wednesday afternoon dismissed ongoing claims of ethnic targeting by security forces — by leaders of the Fulani tribe credited with the attacks — as “propaganda” aimed at frustrating the operations.
